findings.evidence: Grep on FunctionalSpaces finds `theorem ext` only at BesovSpace.lean:362 (the inhomogeneous analogue). The new file has none.
findings.fix: Add `HomogeneousBesovSpace.ext : (∀ j, ((v : lp _ q) j : 𝓢'(E, F)) = ((w : lp _ q) j : 𝓢'(E, F))) → v = w`, ideally `@[ext]`, and use it in the five lemmas above.
findings.issue: `HomogeneousBesovSpace` has no extensionality lemma. `toHomogeneousBesovSpace_eq_iff`, `toHomogeneousBesovSpace_add`, `toHomogeneousBesovSpace_smul`, `coe_toHomogeneousBesovSpace_apply_eq` and `exists_toHomogeneousBesovSpace_eq` each unfold `Subtype.ext (lp.ext (funext …))` and then use `LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.1 Lp.ker_toTemperedDistributionCLM_eq_bot`, so every consumer has to repeat this.

findings.evidence: The only `@[simp]` in the file is at line 274 (`coe_toHomogeneousBesovSpace_apply`). BesovSpace.lean:406-436 tags `toDistr_zero/add/neg/sub/smul` `@[simp]`.
findings.fix: Add `toHomogeneousBesovSpace_zero/neg/sub` and tag them, together with `_add` and `_smul`, `@[simp]`.
findings.issue: The image map is missing its interaction with zero, negation and subtraction. `toHomogeneousBesovSpace_zero`, `_neg` and `_sub` are absent although `MemHomogeneousBesov.zero/neg/sub` exist. The normal-form lemmas `toHomogeneousBesovSpace_add` and `toHomogeneousBesovSpace_smul` are not `@[simp]`.

summary: The block operator stays hidden behind `(rfl)` unfolding lemmas and the predicate API is complete, but the bundled `HomogeneousBesovSpace` and its image map `toHomogeneousBesovSpace` still lack an ext lemma and the simp-tagged lemmas for each operation.
